In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for any class of graphs that is closed under taking subgraphs and has a MSOL-definable treedecomposition, each recognizable graph property is also definable in MSO.
for any graph class $\cal G$ that admits tree decompsitions definable in MSO, every MSO-definable graph class is recognizable in $\cal G$, and every recognizable graph class is definable in $\cal G$.
for every graph class $\mathcal G$ that admits tree decomposable tree decompositions definable in MSO, every recognizable property is definible in MSOL for $\mathcal G$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MSOL-definability is equivalent to recognizability for graphs of bounded degree $k$, where $k$ is a fixed constant.
MSOL-definability equals MSOL-recognizability for bounded degree $k-$outerplanar graphs, Halin graphs and some related classes.
MSOL-definability and recognizability are the same for all graphs of bounded treedepth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for a number of graph classes the complexity of checking graph properties is determined by the complexity of the MSOL expressions that define these properties.
the counting operation in CMSOL can be replaced with a simple counting operation in MSOL for a large number of graph classes.
the counting operation can be omitted in CMSOL expressions for graph properties, which may simplify their description and analysis.
